title: RST rate-limit tracking eviction uses insertion order not staleness
description:
In channel.py lines 331-337 (_check_rst_rate), when _rst_rate_tracking reaches MAX_RST_PEERS (4096), the code evicts the oldest entry by insertion order rather than by timestamp staleness.

Attack scenario:
1. Attacker sends forged RSTs from 4096 spoofed source addresses to fill tracking dict
2. Legitimate peer A is now the 'oldest' entry by insertion
3. Attacker sends more RSTs from new addresses, evicting A
4. Attacker can now send RSTs from A's address at full rate (20/10s) since A has no tracking entry
5. Repeat to bypass per-peer rate limit for targeted peers

The global rate limit (200 RSTs/window) mitigates but doesn't prevent targeted abuse.

Suggested fix: When evicting, prefer entries whose timestamps are all older than window_start (fully stale entries), or use LRU by last timestamp rather than insertion order.

File: src/lichen/coap/secure/channel.py
Lines: 331-337
